segments.text: Your sat-nav says: in fifty metres, turn left.
But on the left, there's a runway. And a jet is coming in to land. What do you do?
Most drivers think: the sat-nav is always right. So you turn left. Onto the runway.
The jet touches down right behind you. And it's catching up. Fast.
Boing! Up you go, onto its roof. And the jet takes off again. Your sat-nav says: recalculating.
Here's how you do it properly.
Stop at the yellow line. And let the jet land first.
Then open the sunroof, grab two baguettes, and wave it in. Like a real marshaller.
Left. A bit more. And stop. Perfect parking. Nose to nose.
The pilot is so impressed, he drops you a bag of peanuts.
And two hundred passengers applaud from the windows.
Next exam question: the crash barrier comes alive. Follow, so you don't miss it.
